text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- Data published by the National Statistics Institute (INE) in reference to 1990 and 1991 says Lisbon region has received less money than Portugal's other regions
- Cement company Cimpor priorities in the next five years will the racionalization of its financial structure and the move to the exterior of 50 percent of its turnover.
- Lisbon's stock exchange launched "Contacto 50" project to create a new market for Small and Medium companies.

- Under-secretary for Transport Guilhermino Rodrigues refutes critics from Portuguese lorry drivers. Lorry drivers protests against government lack of cooperation to help them to recover from losses caused by last month's French lorry drivers strikes.
- The North and the Center of Portugal create employment. Around 100.000 created in the most recent years are private own employment. Agriculture has been the alternative to unemployment.

- Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco wil take to the first Cabinet in January 1997 the dossier "metodos indiciarios" for the calculation of taxes, a Socialist Party (PS) Parliament source told the paper.
- DN/TSF and Euroteste barometer for this month shows ten percent rise in the Right-Wing Popular Party (PP) and a a six percent growth for the Socialist Party (PS).

- Health Ministry and the Chemists National Association agreement to establish a 70 days time limit for the payment of medicines who receive Government's comparticipation may be signed today or Monday, as the paper published on Tuesday.
